subject: RetailX Hosted API: commit increase proposal and soft-throttle safeguards
messages:
From: Devon Park <devon@retailx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@retailx.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API capacity increase — Q4 renewal

Hi Karthik,

We’re kicking off our renewal planning for Q4 and looking at increasing our hosted API commit. Usage during peak promotional windows jumped by ~2.6x this fall and the current soft-throttle behavior caused a few customer-facing errors.

High-level ask: can Redwood provide a proposal for a stepped monthly commit increase (baseline + burst pool) and a guardrail on rate limits that prevents 429 storms while preserving latency? Procurement is sensitive to monthly spend but wants predictable headroom.

Attached is a short usage summary and the current token distribution per route. Happy to jump on a quick call next week.

Thanks,
Devon
Head of Platform Engineering
RetailX

[Attachment: retailx_commit_summary_v3.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@retailx.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity increase — Q4 renewal

Devon — thanks for the context and the summary. We saw the same spike in the telemetry and have a few approaches that balance cost predictability and safety:

1) Stepped monthly commit: Baseline increase of 40% (monthly committed tokens) with an optional scheduled step to +80% in promotional months (can be automated).
2) Burst pool: explicit burst bucket (retailX_burst) that covers short windows with token-based billing above commit but capped per month.
3) Rate-lane soft-throttle: graceful degradation that prioritizes critical routes (checkout, inventory) and returns structured 429 response with retry-after.

I’m attaching a draft rate table showing the unit economics and a sample soft-throttle policy. If you want, Vanessa and I can build a short mutual action plan so Procurement can sign off.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick sync (30m) next Tue/Wed to align on numbers
- Draft amendment (commit + burst + SLAs) for legal review

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_rate_table_q4.csv]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@retailx.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity increase — Q4 renewal

Devon — following up after the internal ops review. A few clarifications from our side that will help Procurement:

- We can offer a 6-month stepped commit with price protection for baseline months and variable billing for burst usage.
- Soft-throttle policy can be customized per route; we recommend prioritizing checkout and recommendations.
- If you want automated step-ups tied to observed usage thresholds, we can include a subscription to our Optimize playbook for continuous suggestions.

If acceptable, we’ll produce an amendment that includes:
- Monthly baseline commit (tokens/month) with two scheduled step dates
- Monthly burst bucket with a hard ceiling and clear per-token billing above commit
- A documented soft-throttle policy and an SLA for max tail latency during bursts

Availability for a 30m call: Tue 12/15 10:00–11:00 or Wed 12/16 14:00–15:30 PST.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Procurement Team <procurement@retailx.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity increase — Q4 renewal

Vanessa / Karthik — thanks. We’re aligned on the stepped commit model in principle but need:

- A clearer monthly spend envelope with worst-case figures (if bursts are fully consumed).
- Explicit rollback / downgrade terms in case we see sustained overprovisioning after promotional periods.
- Evidence that soft-throttle prioritization will not starve checkout traffic (can you share a short test plan or a pinpointed tracer?).

Can you send an updated cost example (worst-case spend + expected) and a proposed clause for downgrade/rollback? Legal will need to see contract language.

Thanks,
Procurement — RetailX

On Tue, Dec 15, 2026 at 10:18 AM PST Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick confirmation on times — we can take Wed 14:00 if that works.
>

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@retailx.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@retailx.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity increase — Q4 renewal

Team — quick update following our call and the ops test we ran with RetailX non-prod traffic:

Summary of agreed items:
- Baseline commit: +45% tokens/month, effective Jan 1 2027 (6-month term).
- Scheduled promotional uplift: automated step to +85% for two calendar weeks (customer-defined windows), with a notification window of 48 hours.
- Burst pool: 120M tokens/month hard ceiling; usage above commit is billed at blended tiered rate (see attached redwood_rate_table_q4.csv).
- Soft-throttle policy: guaranteed prioritization for checkout routes (p95 latency cap + prioritized tokens). Non-critical routes receive structured 429 with retry-after. We validated via a staged replay in non-prod: checkout success rate held at 99.7% during a 3x synthetic spike.
- Downgrade clause: one-time rollback allowed within first 60 days if sustained baseline utilization is <60% for a 30-day window; process requires 30-day notice and mutual sign-off.

Action items:
- Vanessa: draft amendment with the above language and send to RetailX legal (target: EOD Mon 12/21).
- Karthik: include worst-case monthly spend scenarios and a sample clause for the downgrade path (attached).
- Devon: confirm promotional windows and whether you want automated triggers or manual opt-in.

Thanks everyone — happy to keep iterating.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
